newsitem.title: USA: First of America sees $6 mln gain in Q3.
newsitem.headline: First of America sees $6 mln gain in Q3.

text.p: First of America Bank Corp said Monday it expected to record a pre-tax gain of about $6 million in the third quarter related to its sale of credit card receivables.
The bank holding company earlier said it earned $73.2 million, or $0.82 a share, in the second quarter compared with $62.3 million, or $0.67, a year earlier.
During the quarter, the company posted a $1.9 million pre-tax gain on the sale of certain affinity credit card receivables to an issuer specializing in the business.
"We expect to record an additional gain of about $6.0 million pre-tax in the third quarter," said Richard Chormann, First of America's chairman and chief executive.

"The decision to sell a portion of our affinity card portfolio, at such an advantageous price, made good business sense for First of America as it will allow us to concentrate on our core market strategies. We remain committed to our bankcard line of business and the remaining affinity card programs, which continue to be very profitable."
First of America said net charge-offs were $16.2 million during the second quarter, down from $19.9 million in the previous quarter.
Nonperforming assets fell to $109.9 million, or 0.75 percent of total loans plus other real estate owned at June 30, down from $113.7 million at March 31, it said.
